title: 1st CAB Simulated Live Hoist Rooftop Evacuation
description: 1st CAB aviation personnel conduct a simulated live hoist rooftop evacuation as part of exercise Guardian Response 23 at Muscatatuck Training Center May 3, 2023.

transcript.text: Aviation is able to provide rapid
movement of personnel and equipment
supplies around affected areas ,
especially when there's congestion on
the roadways because of evacuations or
damage . Things like that . The
helicopters are able to get into places
that you wouldn't be able to get into
with a vehicle or would take too long
with a vehicle and we're able to do it
much more quickly than vehicles . So
Chinook is the heavy lift cargo
helicopter . It's the biggest
helicopter we have in the army . It
carries the those cargo , we can
configure it a lot of different ways .
The one we're in right now is
configured with the extended range fuel
tanks which allows us to provide
basically a fuel point wherever we want
to put it . So today , for example , we
flew this Chinook out closer to the
disaster area and we were able to
provide advanced fueling
or forward fueling to our medevac
helicopters that were operating out
there as well as a fuel support to
the ground forces . They came by and we
filled up a convoy for them and they
were able to continue their missions
without having to reach back and get
fuel support from trucks . The other
things that Chinook can do , we can
carry up to 33 passengers in one
configuration . We also have the
ability to take our passenger seats out
and put stretchers in . We can carry up
to 22 stretchers and provide
CAS capabilities , which is a lot when
you're doing hospital depression and
things like that . We're able to move a
lot more people than using the Medevac
helicopters which are smaller and can
only carry up to six patients at a time .
Probably the best thing that she gives
us though is its heavy cargo capacity .
So if you look at the inside of this
one , we can fit a lot of cargo inside
of it . And we're also able to sling
loads underneath it , anything from
vehicles to containers , fuel blivets ,
water blivets and we can even
take the cargo net and box up boxes of
M R E s and things like that and move
them , set them down and give them to
whoever needs them . Black Hawk is more ,
it's smaller . We can configure it a
couple of ways . We can either go with
the normal passenger configuration with
the seats in . You have 11 seats , you
can carry 11 people , the Medevac
helicopters , the H H 60
you can either do six ambulatory which
is walking around , able to sit up
right patients , six litter patients or
you can do three and 33 litter , three
ambulatory . So it gives you some
flexibility there . But like I said ,
it's not 22 like you would get in a
Chinook . But the Medevac dedicated
medevac helicopters do have
medical equipment on board like oxygen ,
blood , they're able to transport blood .
They also have dedicated flight medics
that fly along and provide in route
patient care . So that's the advantage
to using the H 60 Medevac helicopter
over just using the Chinook for patient
transfer U H 60 . The Utility Black
Hawk , like I said , you can carry up
to 11 passengers . You can carry cargo
inside it . Not as much . Obviously as
a Black Hawk , you can also sling load
smaller smaller loads than a Black Hawk .
Another advantage once again , going
back to emergency kind of situations is
the Medevac variant does have a hoist .
So we've been using that a lot lately
during this operation to rescue
people that are stranded on rooftops ,
which is really convenient during
floods and hurricanes . The process
starts above us with incident command .
Incident command will receive all the
Taskings and they'll start dividing
them out to all the different task
force that are responding to the
emergency . So they'll send out a
tasking order and they'll decide which
ones can be supported by a ground unit
and which ones need special helicopter
support and then they will start
sending them down to us and we review
them . And if we get the priority based
on the priority and determine which
ones we can support with the assets
that we have currently . And that's how
we task our helicopters with which
emissions they get medevac missions
work similarly . We have a
PEC and I can't remember what the PEC
stands for , but they're in charge of
all the coordination of medical assets .
So they will get a bunch of requests
for evacuations and they'll start
dividing it up into who gets ground
evacuations , who gets helicopter
evacuations . A lot of times it's based
on priority or urgency of
the injuries . And then they'll assign
them down to us . And then after that ,
it works the same way . They will send
us medevac requests and we'll tell them
if we can support or not . And most of
the times we're able to support ,
sometimes we have to turn them away and
they have to send them to ground
because we just ran out of helicopters .
We've been very busy the last couple of
days and sometimes they'll send a
mission to us and we're like , sorry ,
it might be better to send this ground
because we've got three missions
already assigned to each helicopter .
And we don't know when we'll be able to
get to it . So they give us missions ,
we look at it , we do what we can and
sometimes we push back and it's a
little give and take , it's less
concentrated . The good thing about
coming to an exercise like this is
we're able to put all of our attention
and focus on to the mission and we're
able to synchronize and coordinate all
the different parts of our unit back
home . We always have people flying ,
they're always doing training flights .
But what we don't get is the kind of
support aspect of it . Like right now
we have our fuelers are out , they have
the Ford army refueling point set up
and they're providing fuel for the
helicopters . We also have our main CP
set up and we're battle tracking ,
providing mission command . So we're
able to tie those kind of elements ,
support mission command and everything
like that into the flying . Um And
that's how we kind of build our
proficiency and make , make the entire
team better . A lot of the stuff that
we've done here that we don't really
get an opportunity to do as much of .
Um , we've been doing our fire
suppression missions . Our guys are
trained on it but they don't actually
get to do it a lot unless there's gas

somebody will get to actually do it ,
but it's not very often . So here we
have the ability to get some training
for the crews to go and practice
dropping water on fires and forgot to
talk about that with the Chinook . And
the Black Hawk is , we can do
firefighting . We have what we call
bandy buckets . They are big
collapsible orange rubber buckets that

fly , dip them into a lake and then we
fly over the fire and we can fight
wildfires that way . So that's
something we're getting to do here that
we don't necessarily get to do on home

helicopters . That's something we do at
home station , but we don't get to do
enough of it . So here it seems like
each day we've done at least four hoist
missions . So it's really been an
